decisions.reason: The selected Hero V arm geometry is consistent with the existing global visual tone but does not change the brand-expression attributes.
The accent remains deferred and remains defined as deriving from the eventually resolved Hero V; selecting specific Hero V arms does not change that derivation rule.
The second V still derives from the settled Hero V geometry, and the source does not change its role, derivation relationship, identity goal, or development prerequisite.
The source refines only the Hero V arm relationship and does not change the deferred construction or visual language of the remaining wordmark letterforms.
The Hero V geometry choice does not change the deferred champagne-metal material treatment, its qualities, or the sequence requiring geometry to be resolved first.
The source concerns the internal geometry of the Hero V and does not change the deferred complete-wordmark rhythm, kerning, or visual hierarchy.
The source selects and refines the arms' overall geometry but does not establish a new terminal treatment or alter the existing structural, non-decorative terminal rule.
Refining the Hero V geometry does not change the decision to use a proprietary wordmark without a separate icon or monogram.
The source design refinement does not change the obligation to deliver final production-ready artwork.
